_comment: CONTENT-PINNED ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS for skills/skill-authoring/scripts/selfdesc_check.py (round 435, skills B), and read by nothing else. An entry says WHY a claim a data file makes about itself is left standing. `hash` is sha256[:16] of the WHOLE prose field (selfdesc_check.prose_hash): edit the sentence and the acknowledgement expires as J009 rather than muting the artefact forever -- the discipline of state/known-unfilled-placeholders.json and state/known-escalated-diffs.json, and round 349's refusal to allowlist anything unconditionally. An entry matching no finding is reported DEAD and must be DELETED, because an acknowledgement that suppresses nothing reads as coverage. Adding an entry asserts that a round inspected THIS EXACT prose and recorded its reasoning somewhere findable; `why` must name that round's artefact. Prefer FIXING the prose: this file has been EMPTY since round 437, which fixed the one entry round 435 opened it with rather than carrying it. Round 447 corrected the sentence that used to stand here, which still said an entry was present -- and could not have been caught, because `Subject.collections` filtered empty collections out, so a drained list contributed no noun for J005 to count against. It does now.

acknowledged.why: Round 495 (skills B), knowledge/round-495-a-pointer-to-a-scoring-is-not-a-scoring.md section 3. The acknowledged field is prose ABOUT a path that was moved: round 493 committed its bank under a `languages/whence/...` prefix because a stale `cd` persisted into its `mkdir`, then `git mv`d it to the `state/harness/` location the ledger's own `bank` key names, and recorded what had happened. J004 is RIGHT that the cited path does not exist — that is the fact the sentence is reporting. Rewriting the note to stop dangling would delete the only record of the mistake, which is the one thing that makes the episode reusable. Round 493's own state entry reached this conclusion and assigned it here: the note is a note ABOUT the move, so editing it erases the evidence; it wants an entry in the acknowledgement mechanism selfdesc-check already reports against, not a rewrite, and skills(B) owns the acknowledgement. PERMANENT BY CONSTRUCTION, like the ncs_engine.py entry in state/known-dangling-citations.json: a path that was moved away from never comes back, so there is no registry to populate and no fix to wait for. It expires only if someone edits the note, which is the correct trigger to re-inspect. First entry this file has carried since round 437 emptied it. NOTE ON THIS SENTENCE: it deliberately does NOT spell the dangling path, because when it did, this `why` field raised a J004 of its own — the registry that exists to record a broken path could not name the path it was recording. The path is one hop away and fully determined: it is quoted inside the field this entry pins. xref_check solves the same recursion with a declared blind spot over skills/*/scripts/ ('the checkers themselves quote the rot they detect'); the acknowledgement registries have no such exemption, and round 495 chose to name the path by coordinate rather than give them one.
